summary: Halyard mutual NDA with Dutch counterparty edits that widen the Purpose and use right, narrow the carve-outs (deleting independent development), add a 24-month non-solicit, and raise a sub-2-year survival request and a Dutch-law request, while the rest of the template is intact.

findings.quote: VLIET & VAN DER BERG ADVIES B.V., a private company with limited liability
findings.why: The counterparty entity details were filled in with Dutch registration data, which is an entity-detail correction that the lawyer must check against the Dutch Trade Register.

findings.quote: [[INS: potential commercial opportunities, strategic evaluations, advisory engagements, and any other internal or external business activities of the respective Parties from time to time]]
findings.why: The Purpose is widened from a potential commercial relationship to any internal or external business activity, which is effectively no purpose limitation.
findings.draft_redline: The Parties wish to enter into discussions regarding a potential commercial relationship between them (the Purpose).
findings.note_to_counterparty: We need to keep the Purpose tied to our discussions about a potential commercial relationship, so that each side's information is used only for that. We have restored the original wording.

findings.quote: [[INS: or for its internal business assessment, service benchmarking and market evaluation]]
findings.why: The insertion allows use of Confidential Information for the recipient's own internal assessment, benchmarking and market evaluation, beyond the Purpose, and the deletion of 'solely' removes the exclusivity.
findings.draft_redline: not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose;
findings.note_to_counterparty: We cannot agree to use beyond the Purpose, particularly benchmarking or market evaluation using our information. We have reinstated 'solely for the Purpose'.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure
findings.why: The reverse engineering prohibition is retained unchanged.

findings.quote: which is either marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure or would reasonably be considered confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of its disclosure
findings.why: The definition is limited to information disclosed for the Purpose, covers marked or reasonably confidential information and includes derived notes and analyses.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party undertakes to the Disclosing Party that it shall:
findings.why: Obligations are framed by Disclosing Party and Receiving Party, either of which can be either Party, so the NDA is genuinely mutual.

findings.quote: [[INS: (including, in respect of the Counterparty, any groepsmaatschappij within the meaning of Article 2:24b of the Dutch Civil Code)]]
findings.why: The insertion widens the Group definition for the Counterparty only, so Halyard's Group is defined narrowly while the counterparty's may include additional Dutch-law affiliates.
findings.draft_redline: Delete the insertion, or make it apply equally to both Parties.
findings.note_to_counterparty: The Group definition already reaches subsidiaries and holding companies for both Parties. We would prefer a single definition that applies equally to each of us.

findings.quote: [[INS: contemporaneous documentary]]
findings.why: The evidence standard is raised from 'written records or other reasonable evidence' to contemporaneous documentary evidence, which narrows every carve-out.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have kept the evidence standard as 'written records or other reasonable evidence', which is mutual and workable for both of us.

findings.quote: [[INS: as evidenced by the Receiving Party's written records dated prior to the date of this Agreement]]
findings.why: The already-held carve-out is made conditional on written records dated before the Agreement; 'written records' is an acceptable standard but this makes it the only permitted proof, so it narrows the exception.
findings.draft_redline: Delete the inserted words and rely on the evidence standard in clause 3.1.
findings.note_to_counterparty: The evidence standard in clause 3.1 already covers this carve-out, so we have removed the additional wording.

findings.quote: [[DEL: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.]]
findings.why: The independent development carve-out is deleted, so one of the four required exceptions is missing.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We need to keep the independent development exception, which protects both of us. We have reinstated it.

findings.quote: to those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know such Confidential Information
findings.why: Disclosure to Representatives and Group members on a need-to-know basis is permitted and the recipient remains liable for them.

findings.quote: Before making any disclosure pursuant to Clause 5.1, the Receiving Party shall, to the extent that it is legally permitted to do so:
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, with notice and cooperation only where legally permitted and resisting disclosure at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten Business Days of receipt of such request:
findings.why: Return or destruction in ten Business Days, officer-signed confirmation and backup/legal retention exceptions in 6.2 that stay confidential under 6.3.

findings.quote: shall remain the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party (or its licensors, as applicable)
findings.why: Ownership stays with the Disclosing Party and 7.2 grants no licence beyond use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: nothing in this Agreement shall operate or be construed so as to exclude, restrict or limit the liability of either Party in respect of fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation
findings.why: The reliance exclusion is reworded at length but remains mutual and keeps the fraud carve-out, so the substance is unchanged.
findings.fallback_cited: Mutual disclaimers in any reasonable wording.

findings.quote: Nothing in this Agreement shall oblige either Party to disclose any particular information, to enter into any further agreement or transaction with the other Party
findings.why: The no-obligation-to-proceed sentence is retained and 7.3 keeps the as-is and no-warranty position.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, or permit any person to make, any public announcement
findings.why: Mutual publicity restriction requiring prior written consent, with a legal-requirement exception.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement
findings.why: Personal data is limited to business contact details and any further sharing needs a separate DPA or data sharing agreement first.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: A two year term with 30 days' notice to terminate early matches the preferred position.

findings.quote: survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of expiry or termination
findings.why: The text of 10.3 itself is unchanged: three years' survival with indefinite protection only for Trade Secrets.

findings.quote: Our internal policy caps post-termination confidentiality obligations at 18 months from the date of disclosure.
findings.why: The counterparty asks for survival of 18 months measured from disclosure, which is under the 2 year floor and so must be escalated rather than accepted.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We can look at shortening the survival period to no less than two years after expiry or termination, while Trade Secrets stay protected for as long as they remain Trade Secrets. We are not able to go below that.

findings.quote: [[INS: 10.4 During the term of this Agreement and for a period of twenty-four (24) months following its expiry or termination, neither Party shall
findings.why: The new non-solicit runs for the term plus 24 months (over 12), covers consultants, engineers and senior employees without limiting it to staff worked with in discussions, and has no general-advertising exception.
findings.draft_redline: Delete clause 10.4 and the definition of Key Personnel in clause 1.1.9.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We do not usually include a non-solicitation covenant in an NDA of this kind, and the proposed scope and duration go beyond what we can accept. We have deleted it.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Equitable relief is mutual, framed as entitled to seek, and remedies are cumulative under 11.2.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party
findings.why: Assignment requires prior written consent from the other Party, applying to both.

findings.quote: As we are headquartered in Amsterdam, our standard position is for Dutch law and the District Court of Amsterdam (Rechtbank Amsterdam) to apply under Clauses 12.10 and 12.11.
findings.why: The counterparty asks for Dutch law and Amsterdam courts, which is governing law outside England and Wales and must be declined or escalated.
findings.draft_redline: Keep clause 12.10 as drafted. Fallback if required: English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales in clause 12.11.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to move to Dutch law, as we use English law for all our NDAs. We could offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction if that would help.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: The clause text itself is unchanged: English law and exclusive English courts jurisdiction.
